questions.q: Which of the following benefits are likely to accrue to India from the World Trade Organisation? [1995] 1️⃣ India's share in the world trade is to go up from the present 600 million US dollars to 5 billion US dollars by 2000 AD. 2️⃣ It will help boost exports of agricultural commodities from India. 3️⃣ India's share in the world trade is likely to triple by the year 2000 A.D.
questions.e: The WTO attempts to lower trade barriers across nations, which generally increases exports for member nations. While specific dollar projections for 2000 AD were part of contemporary estimates, the primary structural benefits identified were the boost to agricultural exports and the projected increase in world trade share.

questions.q: Local supply of coal is not available to: [1996]
questions.e: VSL Bhadravati, located in Karnataka, is the only major iron and steel plant in India that does not have captive coal mines nearby. It is situated outside the coal-producing area and originally switched to electric furnaces after the completion of the Mahatma Gandhi Hydel Power Station.

questions.q: The number of industries for which industrial licensing is required has now been reduced to: [1997]
questions.e: Industrial licensing was abolished for most industries in the New Industrial Policy of 1991. While the text notes it was reduced to a short list of 18 initially, subsequent reforms reduced this number significantly; by 2015, only five industries remained under compulsory licensing for environmental and strategic reasons.

questions.q: Which of the following places are known for paper manufacturing industry? [1997] 1️⃣ Yamuna Nagar 2️⃣ Guwahati 3️⃣ Shahabad 4️⃣ Ballarpur
questions.e: Yamuna Nagar (Haryana), Guwahati (Assam), and Ballarpur (Maharashtra) are prominent centers for the paper manufacturing industry in India. Shahabad is not primary noted for paper in this context.

questions.q: Scheme of (i) Urban Micro-Enterprises, (ii) Urban Wage Employment and (iii) Housing and Shelter Upgradation are parts of [1997]
questions.e: The Nehru Rozgar Yojana, launched in 1989, was specifically designed to provide employment and support to the urban unemployed and under-employed poor through these three specific components.

questions.q: The contribution of India's small scale sector to the gross turnover in the manufacturing sector since 1992 has been of the order of: [1997]
questions.e: The small-scale industry (SSI) sector is a massive contributor to the Indian economy, accounting for over 40% of the gross turnover in the manufacturing sector and approximately 45% of manufactured exports.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer: List-I (Hazardous industries): A. Glass Industry, B. Brassware Industry, C. Slate Industry, D. Handmade Carpet Industry. List-II (Located at): 1. Moradabad, 2. Marakpur, 3. Ferozabad, 4. Mirzapur. [1997]
questions.e: These industries are traditionally associated with specific clusters: Glass in Firozabad, Brassware in Moradabad, Slate in Marakpur, and Handmade Carpets in Mirzapur. These are often categorized together in discussions regarding child labor and hazardous conditions.

questions.q: The price of any currency in international market is decided by the: [1998] 1️⃣ World Bank 2️⃣ Demand for goods/services provided by the country concerned 3️⃣ Stability of the government of the concerned country 4️⃣ Economic potential of the country in question
questions.e: The market price of a nation's currency is primarily influenced by economic factors like export/import levels (demand for goods/services) and political factors such as the stability of the government.

questions.q: Some time back, the Government of India, decided to de-license 'white goods' industry. 'White goods' include: [1998]
o: soaps, detergents and other mass consumption goods
questions.e: "White goods" traditionally refer to large household electrical appliances like air conditioners and refrigerators which originally featured white enamel finishes. The Government of India de-licensed these items in 1993 to encourage competition and mass consumption.

questions.q: The rough outline map given shows centres of cement industry labelled 1, 2, 3 and 4. Match these centres with the following sets of names: A. Katni, B. Tirunelveli, C. Sikka, D. Churk. [1998]
questions.e: According to the geographical distribution of cement hubs in India: Sikka is in Gujarat (1), Katni is in Madhya Pradesh (2), Churk is in Uttar Pradesh (3), and Tirunelveli is in Tamil Nadu (4).

questions.q: Small-scale industries are, in most cases, not as efficient and competitive as the large-scale ones. Yet the Government provides preferential treatment and reservations in a range of products to the small firms because small-scale industries: 1️⃣ provide higher employment on a per unit capital deployment basis 2️⃣ promote a regional dispersion of industries and economical activities 3️⃣ have performed better in export of manufactured products than the large scale ones 4️⃣ provide jobs to low-skill workers, who otherwise may not find employment avenues elsewhere [1998]
questions.e: The government supports SSIs because they have a low capital-output ratio, meaning they generate more employment per unit of investment and help in the regional dispersal of economic activity using local raw materials.

questions.q: From the balance sheet of a company, it is possible to: [1999]
o: assess the profitability and size of the company
determine the size and composition of the assets and liabilities of the company
determine the market share, debts and assets of the company
judge the extent of profitability of this company
questions.e: A balance sheet is a "snapshot" of a company's financial condition at a specific date, listing its assets, liabilities, and ownership equity. It primarily shows the financial position rather than a long-term judge of profitability (which is usually found in a P&L statement).

questions.q: Match List-I (Industries) with List-II (Industrial Centres): A. Pearl fishing, B. Automobiles, C. Ship building, D. Engineering goods. List-II: 1. Pune, 2. Tuticorin, 3. Pinjore, 4. Marmagao. [1999]
questions.e: Specific industrial hubs in India include Tuticorin for Pearl fishing, Pune for the Automobile industry, Marmagao for Ship building, and Pinjore for Engineering goods.

questions.q: The product life cycle from inception to demise is shown in the graph. Match List I (Stage) with List II (Sales/Profit): A. Product Development, B. Maturity, C. Growth, D. Introduction. [1999]
questions.e: The product life cycle theory, developed by Raymond Vernon, tracks a product through stages: Development (Investment/Loss), Introduction (Slow Sales), Growth (Rising Profits), and Maturity (Peak Sales/Stable Profits).

questions.q: Industrial development in India, to an extent, is constrained by: 1️⃣ lack of adequate entrepreneurship and leadership in business 2️⃣ lack of savings to invest 3️⃣ lack of technology, skills and infrastructure 4️⃣ limited purchasing power among the larger masses [1999]
questions.e: While entrepreneurship exists, the primary structural constraints on Indian industrial growth have been low investment savings, gaps in infrastructure and technology, and the limited purchasing power of the general population.

questions.q: Tourism industry in India is quite small compared to many other countries in terms of India's potential size. Which one of the following statements is correct in this regard? [1999]
o: Distances in India are too far apart and luxury hotels are too expensive for western tourists.
For most of months India is too hot for western tourists to feel comfortable.
Most of the picturesque resorts in India such as in the North East and Kashmir are, for all practical purposes, out of bounds.
In India, the infrastructure required for attracting tourists is inadequate.
questions.e: Although India is a preferred destination due to its rich culture and monuments, the growth of the tourism sector is primarily hampered by inadequate infrastructure (transport, connectivity, facilities).

questions.q: Match List-I (Industrial Unit) with List-II (Centre): A. Atlas Cycle Company Ltd., B. Bharat Earth Movers Ltd., C. Indian Farmers Fertilizers Co-operative Ltd., D. National Aluminium Company Ltd. List-II: 1. Bangalore, 2. Bhubaneswar, 3. Kalol, 4. Sonepat. [1999]
questions.e: Atlas Cycle is based in Sonepat (Haryana), BEML is in Bangalore (Karnataka), IFFCO has a major plant in Kalol (Gujarat), and NALCO is headquartered in Bhubaneswar (Odisha).

questions.q: Assertion (A): Information technology is fast becoming a very important field of activity in India. Reason (R): Software is one of the major exports of the country and India has a very strong base in hardware. [1999]
o: Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
questions.e: While Information Technology is indeed a booming sector (A is true), the reason is flawed because India's strength lies primarily in software services, while its hardware base has historically been considered relatively weak or normal compared to global leaders.

questions.q: Consider the following factors regarding an industry: 1️⃣ Capital investment 2️⃣ Business turnover 3️⃣ Labour force 4️⃣ Power consumption. Which of these determine the nature and size of the industry? [2001]
questions.e: The nature and size of an industry are generally determined by its capital investment, the volume of business turnover, and its power consumption patterns.

questions.q: Assertion (A): India's software exports increased at an average growth rate of 50% since 1995-96. Reason (R): Indian software companies were cost-effective and maintained international quality. [2001]
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.e: India's massive growth in software exports was driven by the competitive advantage of being cost-effective while delivering high-quality products that met international standards.

questions.q: Consider the following states: 1️⃣ Gujarat 2️⃣ Karnataka 3️⃣ Maharashtra 4️⃣ Tamil Nadu. The descending order of these states with reference to their level of Per Capita Net State Domestic Product is: [2001]
questions.e: Based on economic data from that period, the descending order of per capita income (NSDP) among these industrialized states was Maharashtra, followed by Gujarat, Karnataka, and then Tamil Nadu.

questions.q: With reference to the Public Sector Undertakings in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Minerals and Metals Trading Corporation of India Limited is the largest non-oil importer of the country 2️⃣ Project and Equipment Corporation of India Limited is under the Ministry of Industry 3️⃣ One of the objectives of Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Limited is to enforce quality control and compulsory pre-shipment inspection of various exportable commodities [2002]
questions.e: MMTC is indeed India's largest international trading company and the largest non-oil importer. Statement 2 is incorrect as PEC falls under the Ministry of Commerce. Statement 3 is incorrect because ECGC provides credit risk insurance, not quality inspection.

questions.q: HINDALCO, an aluminium factory located at Renukut owes its site basically to: [2002]
questions.e: HINDALCO's location at Renukut is primarily due to the abundant supply of power from the Rihand Dam (NTPC) and its own captive power plants, as aluminium smelting is a highly power-intensive process.

questions.q: Which one of the following committees recommended the abolition of reservation of items for the small scale sector in industry? [2003]
questions.e: The Abid Hussain Committee (1997) recommended the total de-reservation of items for the SSI sector, suggesting that a policy of promotion and strengthening should replace the policy of reservation.

questions.q: With reference to India, which one of the following statements is NOT correct? [2003]
o: IPCL is India's largest petrochemical company
RIL is the largest private sector company in India
BSNL is the first telecom service organization in India to launch a nationwide cellular service at one time
questions.e: Statement (a) is incorrect because ONGC is actually India's largest petrochemical company, while IPCL is the second largest.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct? [2003]
o: India is the second largest producer of silk in the world.
India ranks third in the world in coal production.
India is the second largest producer of nitrogenous fertilizers in the world.
India is the ninth largest steel producing country in the world.
questions.e: Statement (b) is incorrect; as of the text's data, India was the third largest steel producer in the world. It is the second largest in silk (after China) and nitrogenous fertilizers.

questions.q: During the year 2000-01 which one of the following Industries recorded the highest growth rate in India? [2003]
questions.e: In the year 2000-01, the steel industry recorded a growth rate of 7%, which was higher than electricity (4%) and coal (3.3%).

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct? [2003]
o: It is the function of Directorate General of Civil Aviation to plan and construct runways and terminal buildings and to provide air safety services
The Airports Authority of India manages seven of the country's international airports
The Airports Authority of India is the regulatory organisation for enforcing civil air regulations in India
Alliance Air is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Indian Airlines
questions.e: Alliance Air was formed in 1996 as a completely owned subsidiary of Indian Airlines. The DGCA is the regulator, while AAI handles infrastructure (not the other way around).

questions.q: Assertion (A): India does not export natural rubber. Reason (R): About 97% of India's demand for natural rubber is met from domestic production. [2004]
o: Both A and R are true but R is NOT a correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is false but R is true
questions.e: India is a major producer of natural rubber, but because domestic consumption is extremely high (the 4th largest consumer globally), it exports very little. The statement that it does "not export" at all is technically false as small quantities are exported for better pricing.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Balance of Payments represents a better Picture of a country economic transactions with the rest of the world than the Balance of Trade Reason (R): Balance of Payments takes into account the exchange of both visible and invisible items whereas balance of Trade does not. [2006]
o: Both 'A' and 'R', are individually true and 'R' is the correct explanation of 'A'.
Both 'A' and 'R' are individually true but 'R' is not the correct explanation of 'A'.
questions.e: Balance of Payments (BoP) is more comprehensive because it includes visible trade, invisible services (remittances, tourism), and capital transfers, whereas Balance of Trade only looks at the export and import of physical goods.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is not correct? [2005]
o: Visakhapatnam Steel Plant is a unit of the Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd.
Maharashtra Elektrosmelt Ltd. is a subsidiary of the Steel Authority of India Ltd.
Salem Steel Plant is a premier producer of stainless steel in India.
Rourkela Steel Plant, the first integrated steel plant in the Public Sector of India was set up with the Soviet Union collaboration.
questions.e: Statement (a) is incorrect because the Rourkela Steel Plant was set up with German collaboration, not Soviet Union collaboration (the Soviet Union collaborated on Bhilai).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ MMTC Limited is India's largest international trading organization. 2️⃣ Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited has been set up by MMTC jointly with the Government of Orissa. [2009]
questions.e: MMTC is indeed the largest international trading organization in India. It also partnered with the Government of Odisha (IPICOL) to promote Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited.

questions.q: Which one of the following sets of commodities are exported to India by arid and semi-arid countries in the Middle East? [2009]
questions.e: Middle Eastern countries, due to their arid climate, are major exporters of specific agricultural products like dates (fruits) and palm oil to the Indian market.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a feature of Limited Liability Partnership firm? [2010]
o: Partnership and management need not be separate
Internal governance may be decided by mutual agreement among partners
It is corporate body with perpetual succession
questions.e: In an LLP, there is no upper limit on the number of partners, unlike a traditional partnership which is limited to 20 partners.

questions.q: In India, which of the following, is regulated by the Forward Markets Commission? [2010]
o: Both Commodities Futures and Financial Futures Trading
questions.e: The Forward Markets Commission (FMC) was the chief regulator of commodity futures and forwards in India until its merger with SEBI. It regulated commodity trade across various exchanges.

questions.q: What is/are the recent policy initiative(s) of Government of India to promote the growth of manufacturing sector? 1️⃣ Setting up of National Investment and Manufacturing Zones 2️⃣ Providing the benefit of 'single window clearance' 3️⃣ Establishing the Technology Acquisition and Development Fund [2012-1]
questions.e: All three initiatives are core components of the National Manufacturing Policy, which aims to increase the manufacturing sector's share in GDP and create jobs through better infrastructure and simplified clearances.

questions.q: In India, in the overall Index of Industrial Production, the Indices of Eight Core Industries have a combined weight of 37.90%. Which of the following are among those Eight Core Industries? 1️⃣ Cement 2️⃣ Fertilizers 3️⃣ Natural gas 4️⃣ Refinery products 5️⃣ Textiles [2012-1]
questions.e: The Eight Core Industries are Coal, Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Refinery Products, Fertilizers, Steel, Cement, and Electricity. Textiles is not one of the eight core industries.

questions.q: Despite having large reserves of coal, why does India import millions of tonnes of coal? 1️⃣ It is the policy of India to save its own coal reserves for future, and import it from other countries for the present use. 2️⃣ Most of the power plants in India are coal-based and they are not able to get sufficient supplies of coal from within the country. 3️⃣ Steel companies need large quantity of coking coal which has to be imported. [2012-1]
questions.e: India imports coal because domestic supply often falls short of the demand from power plants and because Indian coal is largely non-coking, requiring the import of high-quality coking coal for steel production.

questions.q: The balance of payments of a country is a systematic record of [2013-1]
o: economic transaction between the government of one country to another
capital movements from one country to another.
good exported from a country during a year
all import and export transactions of a country during a given period of time, normally a year
questions.e: Balance of Payments is a comprehensive accounting record of all monetary/economic transactions between a country and the rest of the world, including trade in goods, services, and financial capital.

questions.q: Which one among the following industries is the maximum consumer of water in India? [2013-1]
questions.e: Thermal power plants are the largest industrial consumers of water in India, primarily using it for cooling and to generate steam to drive turbines.

questions.q: Disguised unemployment generally means [2013-1]
o: large number of people remain unemployed
marginal productivity of labour is zero
questions.e: Disguised unemployment occurs when more people are working than necessary; hence, if some workers are removed, total production remains unchanged because their marginal productivity is zero.

questions.q: With reference to Balance of Payments, which of the following constitutes/constitute the Current Account? 1️⃣ Balance of trade 2️⃣ Foreign assets 3️⃣ Balance of invisibles 4️⃣ Special Drawing Rights [2014-1]
questions.e: The Current Account of the BoP includes the Balance of Trade (goods) and the Balance of Invisibles (services, transfers, income). Foreign assets and SDRs fall under the Capital or Financial accounts.

questions.q: In India, the steel production industry requires the import of [2015-1]
questions.e: Coking coal is a vital ingredient in the steel-making process. Since most coal found in India is non-coking, the steel industry relies heavily on imports.

questions.q: In the 'Index of Eight Core Industries', which one of the following is given the highest weight? [2015-1]
questions.e: Among the eight core industries, electricity generation historically holds the highest weight (around 10.32% of the IIP), followed by steel and refinery products.

questions.q: Which of the following brings out the 'Consumer Price Index Number for Industrial Workers"? [2015-1]
o: The Department of Personnel and Training
questions.e: The Labour Bureau, an attached office of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, is responsible for compiling and releasing the CPI for Industrial Workers.

questions.q: Recently, India's first 'National Investment and Manufacturing Zone' was proposed to be set up in [2016-1]
questions.e: The first NIMZ was proposed in the Prakasam district of Andhra Pradesh as part of the "Make in India" campaign.

questions.q: With reference to pre-packaged items in India, it is mandatory to the manufacturer to put which of the following information on the main label, as per the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011? 1️⃣ List of ingredients including additives 2️⃣ Nutrition information 3️⃣ Recommendations, if any, made by the medical profession about the possibility of any allergic reactions 4️⃣ Vegetarian/non-vegetarian [2016-1]
questions.e: Under the FSSAI regulations of 2011, manufacturers must include ingredients, nutritional info, and the veg/non-veg logo. Medical recommendations regarding allergies are not a mandatory labeling requirement in this specific context.

questions.q: With reference to 'Quality Council of India (QCI)', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ QCI was set up jointly by the Government of India and the Indian Industry. 2️⃣ Chairman of QCI is appointed by the Prime Minister on the recommendations of the industry to the Government. [2017-1]
questions.e: The QCI is a public-private partnership set up to establish and operate national accreditation structures. Its chairman is appointed by the PM based on industry recommendations.

questions.q: India enacted The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999 in order to comply with the obligations to [2018-1]
questions.e: The GI Act of 1999 was enacted to meet India's obligations under the TRIPS agreement of the World Trade Organization (WTO).

questions.q: Consider the following countries: 1️⃣ Australia 2️⃣ Canada 3️⃣ China 4️⃣ India 5️⃣ Japan 6️⃣ USA. Which of the above are among the 'free-trade partners' of ASEAN? [2018-1]
questions.e: ASEAN's free-trade partners (often cited in RCEP context) include China, India, Japan, South Korea, Australia, and New Zealand. Canada and the USA are not ASEAN FTA partners.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The quantity of imported edible oils is more than the domestic production of edible oils in the last five years. 2️⃣ The Government does not impose any customs duty on all the imported edible oils a special case. [2018-1]
questions.e: India is the world's largest importer of edible oils, and imports consistently exceed domestic production. Statement 2 is incorrect because the government does impose customs duties to protect domestic farmers.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Coal sector was nationalized by the Government of India under Indira Gandhi. 2️⃣ Now, coal blocks are allocated on lottery basis. 3️⃣ Till recently, India imported coal to meet the shortages of domestic supply, but now india is self-sufficient in coal production. [2019-1]
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct (nationalization in 1973). Statement 2 is wrong because blocks are allocated via auction. Statement 3 is wrong because India still imports millions of tonnes of coal.

questions.q: With reference to Foreign Direct Investment in India, which one of the following is considered its major characteristics? [2020-1]
o: It is the investment made by foreign institutional investors in the Government securities.
It is the investment through capital instruments essentially in a listed company.
It is largely non-debt creating capital flow.
It is the investment which involves debt-servicing.
questions.e: FDI is preferred because it is non-debt creating (unlike loans) and brings in long-term capital and technology. It can occur in both listed and unlisted companies.

questions.q: With reference to the international trade of India at present, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ India's merchandise exports are less than its merchandise imports. 2️⃣ India's imports of iron and steel, chemicals, fertilisers and machinery have decreased in recent years. 3️⃣ India's exports of services are more than its imports of services. 4️⃣ India suffers from an overall trade/current account deficit. [2020-1]
questions.e: India historically runs a merchandise trade deficit (Imports > Exports) and a services trade surplus (Exports > Imports). However, the merchandise deficit usually outweighs the service surplus, leading to an overall current account deficit.

questions.q: With reference to Trade-Related Investment Measures (TRIMS), which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ Quantitative restrictions on imports by foreign investors are prohibited. 2️⃣ They apply to investment measures related to trade in both goods and services. 3️⃣ They are not concerned with the regulation of foreign investment. [2020-1]
questions.e: TRIMs applies strictly to trade in goods only (not services). It prohibits measures that restrict trade, such as quantitative restrictions, but does not regulate the investment itself.
